propositions: Completion verifier trips RunawayToolLoopError while re-reading cached evidence files, despite prior memoization fix, blocking legitimate closes.
The runaway guard layer sits outermost and counts memo-served (free, cached) repeats as loop evidence, defeating the memoization layer's cost optimization.
Guard and memo layers conflict: memo makes repeats cheap but guard punishes them by counting distinct-ratio over all calls, not just executed work.
Solution recomposes guard and memo via a shared ToolCallLedger that tracks only executed (non-memoized) calls for ratio computation, plus a served-streak backstop for pure cache-loop detection.
Memo layer records executed work at five sites (passthrough, cache miss, path-unparseable read, first-read fetch, truncated-window fallback) but never on cache-served paths.
